d: Garden of Esperia. Discord comes out of Hell, enters the garden, complains that she is not called to the wedding of Teti, resolves to avenge it, kidnaps the golden apple, and then flying away. Discord.
The summit of Mount Pelio. Silvio's reason for the loving inconstance, recognizes the place of the loving pleasures with Eurilla; he sees it, and withdraws to listen to it. Silvio.
He expresses Eurilla, who is not happier, than being in love. Silvio meets her, takes her time in which to console her pains, and confirms her perseverance. Eurilla, Silvio.

Eurilla assures Silvio of his correspondence in Love, and consoles him with hope. Lucan, listening to their reasonings, reprimands Eurilla for the course of faith. Eurilla confirms his promises. Silvio complains about it, and is consoled by Eurilla, who discovering herself in love with both, declares how they must love her. Lucano, and Silvio complain about the judgment of Eurilla. Lucano resorts to deception: but realizing himself, being by the lower gods, set up the banquet, for the wedding of Teti, they leave separately. Eurilla, Silvio, Lucano.

Discord descends, and discourses, that there is not the sweetest thing, but revenge. Coming forward, that the gods appear, they already sit at the table: they hide to throw you over the apple. Discord.

The lower gods, who have the table, sing, under the figure of allegory, in praise of the serene spouses. Discordia gives out the pomo, and then goes away. Juno, Pallade, and Venus come to the contest, for the purchase of the pomo; they resort to the sentence of Jupiter, and he puts the case back to the judge of Paris. A cloud comes down from heaven, into which the gods enter, and by the commandment of Jupiter, led by the air by Mercury, they go out into the Phrygia to find it. With the dance that follows among the other gods, who remain, the first end. Chorus of the lower gods, Jupiter, Apollo, Mercury, Junone, Pallade, Venus, who sing; Discord hidden. All the other gods, and gods, who do not sing.

Bosco in Mount Ida. Enone reminds herself of Love, which leads to Paris. He expresses, that for such a beautiful cause every torment may be gentle; and from his own pains, he makes arguments to make his constancy impenetrable. He sees Paride coming, and meets him. Enone.

Paride, and Enone establish an entire, and full firmness to their loves. Enone departs. Paride remains, and rejoices to be Enone's lover. He exclaims the might of Love, and how one should love: consoling himself in the ardor of those flames, which gently consumes his chest. Coming down Mercury, Juno, Pallas, and Venus from heaven, he is surprised by a sudden astonishment. Paride, Enone.

Paride receives from Mercury the commissions of Jupiter, and is arranged for judgment. Juno, and Pallade, expressed their reasons, tempted in vain his perseverance; disdained they depart. Venus obtained victoriously the pome, consoles him with the hope of the purchase of Helena; and he, driven by new loving stimuli, resolves to abandon Enone, and reveal himself to his father; and transferred to the court of Sparta, kidnapped Elena to Greeks. With the dance of Pastors, which follows, ends the second act. Mercury, Juno, Pallas, Venus, Paris.
Shepherd Lippo, complains about the bitter deceptions, and the cruelty of his nymph; consolation with singing. Lippo.

Enone grieves bitterly over Paride's sudden departure. He consoles her with words, expressing Love, and faith. They talk about the effects of hope. Paride starts. Enone regrets, and resolves that he never lacks faith, though far away, to his sweetest Paris. Enone, Paris.

Cerispo, Nympheo, Corimbo children, who came to the challenge over the owl's game, found the right place, attack the game. Overcoming a bear intralasciano to play, and fleeing put an end to the third act. Cerispo, Nympheo, Corimbo.
Wood above the shore of Sparta, with sea in the distance. Paride arrives at the coast of Sparta, descends from the ship, and commanded 'compañeros, who wait for his return, enters the wood. Paris.

He parides, hearing the horn, and the voice of a hunter, who approaches him, stops, and pretends to sleep. Melindo hunter arrives, and sings over the delight of the hunt, and being loaded with prey he starts again towards the city: he plays the horn, and Paride pretends to wake up, complaining that his rest is interrupted. Melindo approaches him, and asks him who he is. Paride says, being Dorindo musico, born of Tarso, city of Cilicia, left to go to the court of the king of Cyprus: but that assaulted the ship from a fierce storm, saved himself swimming, finally reached that litte, and while he regrets, Melindo consoles him, and leads him to the court to present him to Elena. Paride, Melindo.

Rooms of Elena. Elena expresses the sweetness, and the strength of Love; Argenia bitterness, and vanity. Elena appreciates the flames; Argenia despises them, one establishes to live loving, and the other to flee Love. Elena, Argenia.

Melindo presents Paris to Elena. Love descended from heaven, lightning, and one, and the other, and then hides. They fall in love with the same point. Helen marvels at it, and asks Paris who he is. Paris takes more time, and other place to discover. They praise music, and Paris sing. Helen, feeling more in love, invites Paride to stop, and star in his court. Helena, Argenia, Paris, Melindo.
Courtyard. Lupino staffiero looks for Serina bridesmaid of court, whose beauty praises. But not content to praise, or the hairs, or the eyes, or the mouth, stops over the praises of the nose. Lupino.

Ancrocco sweeper of court, revealed to Lupino to be in love. They agree to sing together: but not being able to Ancrocco, to be singing, to equalize the song of Lupino, Lupino disdained starts. Ancrocco picks up the song, and singingly expresses his loves. Ancrocco, Lupino.

Helena's remote rooms. Elena, retreating into the most remote rooms, exhibits the flames she feels for Paris, which she believed Dorindo, and resumes her own ailments, which oblige the enjoyment of the most sublime loves, run to bow down such a low object. Helena.

Paride passes through the rooms of Helena, and is taken up by her: but undisputed prince, and in love, asks for forgiveness of the boldness, and refreshment to the ardor. Elena won by so powerful assault, jumping over the bed, makes her loving arms chain to the neck of Paride; and while giving to kisses, Love tightens the curtains, and leaves the room. Paride, Elena.
Love expresses its might, and then flying you go. Love.
Garden with loggias. Argenia sings over the vanity of lovers. Argenia.
Draspo gardener discovers his flames in Argenia, and after being mocked by her, they both depart separately. Draspo, Argenia.

Piazza del Temple di Venus. Paride arrives at the island of Cythera, and waits for Elena outside the temple of Venus. Elena leaves the temple, and Paris kidnaps her. With a overthrow of Trojans, and Greeks, where the Greeks, yielding to the strength of the Trojans, after an obstinate battle, finally take charge, finishes the Fourth Act. Paride singing, Elena, Trojans, and Greeks who do not sing.
Fiumara in the countryside of Troy. Enone expresses the torments, and the jealousy she feels for the distance of her dearest Paris; and consoles herself with hope. Enone.

Horon the Messenger of Paris, walking in reverse Troy, to give, to Priam of the robbery of Helena, and of the arrival of both, he meets in Enone, from which he is taught the way. Enone, talking with Oronte, means the return of Paris, and rejoices: but upon arriving Oronte, who will arrive with Helena, he turns in a moment the joy in mourning. Oronte followed with every prestitude his journey; and she anxious to understand more distinctly the success, goes after him to reach him. Oronte, Enone.

A remote street of the city, with trees and ruins. Ergaurus the servant of Medoro, while he brings the wine to the master, thirsting for him, tries to open the box, in which are locked the vial; and not being able to open it is disdainful. Open it at last, taste the wine, and find it to be sweet, drink little by little, which eventually gets drunk. Ergaurus.

Bookshop. Medoro tutor of pages, teaches Irseno, and Ermillo. Instead of learning the lesson, he contemplates the fabulous figures of Exopus. Medoro takes him up again: but in response, they respond, that to be noble, it is not necessary to study him, mocking him, they leave. Medoro, Irseno, Ermillo.
Medoro, grieving to be mocked, speaks over virtue, and over nobility. Medoro.
Portico with garden in the distance. Enone, having not been able to reach the messenger, also reaches the court, to find him. Enone.

Irsen, and Ermillo see Enone, and enamored of her beauty, they try to kidnap her: but when they come to contend over the election of the place, where they must lead her, Enone comes out of his hands. At last came to arms, Ermillo is wounded, and feeling close to dying, sorrows of his misfortune, not knowing who to receive comfort. Irsen, Ermillo, Enone.

Ergaurus, having with his sleep released the drunkenness, with a bottle of wine in his hand, expresses his contentment. He listens to the laments of Ermaurus, and moved by compassion, consoles him with wine. Ermaurus drinks, and got back somewhat the vital spirits, leaning on Ergaurus' arm, we start. Ergaurus, Ermaurus.

Priamo's rooms. Prior to receiving the notice of the return of Paris, and of the robbery of Helena, he gives information to Ecuba, and filled with rejoicing go to give the necessary orders, so that the wedding may be prepared. Priamo, Ecuba.
Ecuba's antechamber. Filinda maid rejoices to be in love, and praises the sweetness of love. Filinda.

Enone, to be no longer molested by the pages, clothed as a boy, is looking for the messenger; Filinda deceived by the garment falls in love with it, they are talking together, and Enone, pretending to be persuaded, promises to love her. Enone, Filinda.

Hermillo pardons Irsen; with Ergaurus he causes to see the wound: but not finding himself in Ermillo other wound, that the impression, Irsen rejoices, and with it he part. Ergaurus is stunned, and stunned of the foolishness of Ermillo, and having intended to approach the time of the wedding of Paris, with Elena, he establishes to porger also to himself. Ermillo, Irsen, Ergauro.
Paride arrives, and Elena in Troy, Enone sees him, and regrets. Paride, Elena, Enone.
Enone is bitterly sorry that she was abandoned by Paris, and after a lamentable exaggeration she starts; determined to die, not to live in constant torment. Enone.

The Royal Hall. Priam, and Ecuba, accompanied by all the other Princes, Trojan princesses, praise the beauty of Helena, and she devotes herself to amenues for a daughter. She expresses the loss made of her kingdom to follow Paris; and Priam, promising her greater empire, grants her to Paris as wife. With the dance, which then follows Princes and Princesses, the fifth act ends, and all the work together. Priam, Ecuba, Paris, Helena, all the other Princes, and Princesses who do not sing.
